Sources, credits, and the figures left out.

A civic guide is only as good as its paper trail. This page records where the facts, maps, and photographs come from, and where the official record disagrees with itself.

Checked 2026-11-20. The checked date is not the same as a source's own as-of date.

On this page Figure notesSource registrySource groupsMap generationPhotograph creditsOpen gaps

Two figures not published here.

The Municipality of Ibaan publishes two profile pages. They do not agree on elevation or on the distance to Manila. Rather than choose one silently, this guide leaves both out.

Elevation

The municipal profile gives 178 metres above sea level. The geography section of the same site gives 124 metres. This guide leaves both out until the municipality resolves the discrepancy.

Distance to Manila

The municipal profile gives 96 kilometres. The geography section gives 118 kilometres. This guide leaves both out and keeps the shorter, consistent distance to Batangas City: 13 kilometres.

The distance to Batangas City, 13 kilometres, appears in the municipal profile and does not conflict across the two pages. It is the only distance figure used on this site.

Map boundaries

The barangay map uses detailed OCHA COD-AB boundaries from NAMRIA and PSA, released 2023-11-06 and redistributed with PSGC codes by faeldon/philippines-psgc-shapefiles. The Batangas context map uses a simplified PSA/NAMRIA file from barangay-boundaries-repository. Both are orientation aids, not survey work.

  • Detailed barangay boundaries ↗
  • Simplified context boundaries ↗

Interactive map tiles

The interactive map loads OpenStreetMap data through OpenFreeMap vector tiles. Its 3D view also requests elevation tiles from the Mapzen Terrain Tiles dataset on AWS. Those services receive ordinary tile requests when a reader opens the map; this site has no analytics or user accounts. The 3D view shows real terrain and building height, not population or land-area figures.

  • OpenFreeMap ↗
  • OpenStreetMap copyright ↗
  • Mapzen Terrain Tiles on AWS ↗

Map generation

Source

OCHA COD-AB boundaries from NAMRIA and PSA, released 2023-11-06 and redistributed with PSGC codes by faeldon/philippines-psgc-shapefiles. Upstream data is CC BY-IGO 3.0; the redistribution wrapper is MIT.

Detail

The barangay outlines keep their source vertex detail, so they follow the mapped shapes rather than coarse tiles. The Batangas context map remains simplified. Neither map is for measuring land, settling jurisdiction, or drawing a legal boundary.

Interactive map

The 26 barangay polygons are overlaid on OpenStreetMap data served by OpenFreeMap. The 3D view also requests terrain and building data. No figure on this site is encoded in the height of the map.

Flat fallback

If WebGL or the tile services are unavailable, the page keeps a plain SVG outline of the same 26 barangays. The flat view is also one click away in the map toolbar.

Where the record stops

    Could not verify

    Not published
